task.title: Stage 2 appraisal safety contract document
task.objective: Write a specification document (docs/stage2_appraisal_safety_contract.md) that explicitly defines what constitutes safe appraisal deepening versus dangerous narrative drift, the preconditions for granting any new tick live LLM authority, and the monitoring gates Stage 2 must continuously pass.
exact_scope: Create docs/stage2_appraisal_safety_contract.md with the following sections:
1. Safe vs Unsafe appraisal deepening: define at least 3 concrete criteria distinguishing safe appraisal deepening from dangerous narrative drift, with examples of each

2. Per-tick authority preconditions: for each of the 8 ticks (T1–T8), specify whether it currently has live authority and, for each deferred tick, list the concrete preconditions that must hold before it can gain live LLM authority

3. Monitoring gates: define numeric thresholds for at least 5 monitoring gates that Stage 2 must continuously satisfy, referencing actual infrastructure (audit_drift.py, degradation_tracker.py, appraisal_audit_log.py)
4. Graduated response: define escalation levels (warn → fallback → halt) with specific trigger conditions tied to the monitoring gates
5. Anti-patterns / forbidden approaches: list known anti-patterns that Stage 2 must not adopt, consistent with decisions_summary.md
acceptance_criteria: docs/stage2_appraisal_safety_contract.md exists and is well-structured markdown
Section on safe vs unsafe defines at least 3 concrete criteria with examples distinguishing safe appraisal deepening from dangerous narrative drift
Per-tick authority table covers all 8 ticks (T1–T8) with current status and, for each deferred tick, specific preconditions for gaining live authority
At least 5 monitoring gates are defined with concrete numeric thresholds (no TBD or placeholder values)
Monotonic drift gate correctly states: warn at >=10 consecutive days, fail at >=20 consecutive days (matching audit_drift.py build_dimension_verdict with default monotonic_window=10)
No graduated response level references detection of monotonic spans shorter than 10 days, since detect_monotonic_drift(window=10) cannot flag spans below 10 days
Graduated response defines at least 3 escalation levels with trigger conditions tied to the defined monitoring gates
Anti-patterns section is consistent with decisions_summary.md (LLM cannot write ledger, AppraisalSignal v1 frozen, T4 frozen except via 26B, etc.)
All threshold values referenced in the document are verifiable against actual source code in back/tools/audit_drift.py and back/app/llm/degradation_tracker.py
All existing tests pass with no regressions (python -m pytest tests/ -v from back/)
non_goals: No source code changes — this task produces only a markdown document
No implementation of monitoring gates or enforcement logic
No changes to the degradation tracker, audit tools, or any engine code
No expansion of live LLM authority to any currently deferred tick
No redesign of the appraisal pipeline or settlement architecture
No player influence or world-generator changes
constraints: All numeric thresholds in monitoring gates MUST be verified against the actual source code — in particular: audit_drift.py::build_dimension_verdict uses `status = 'fail' if longest['length'] >= monotonic_window * 2 else 'warn'` with default monotonic_window=10, meaning: spans >=10 days = warn, spans >=20 days = fail. detect_monotonic_drift only flags spans where streak_len >= window (>=10 days); spans shorter than 10 days are invisible to the tool.
The graduated response levels must only reference detection capabilities that actually exist in the current tooling — do not invent warn ranges for span lengths the tools cannot detect
AppraisalSignal v1 is frozen — the document must not propose changes to its field definitions
LLM does not write ledger — this principle must be preserved in all safety criteria
T4 relational residual activation is frozen — the only approved unfreeze path is Phase 26B via social event-aware activation
Stage 1 bridge scope is T1/T2/T4 only — document must not grant deferred ticks (T3/T5/T6/T7/T8) live authority; it defines what preconditions they must meet first
The document is a specification, not implementation — it defines WHAT must hold, not code to enforce it
review_focus: CRITICAL: Verify that every numeric threshold in the document matches the actual source code — especially the monotonic drift gate (warn >=10, fail >=20) and any degradation rate thresholds from degradation_tracker.py
CRITICAL: Verify that no graduated response level references detection capabilities that do not exist in the current tooling (e.g., no monotonic span detection below 10 days)
Check that per-tick preconditions for deferred ticks are concrete and specific, not vague aspirational statements
Verify anti-patterns are consistent with decisions_summary.md and CLAUDE.md hard rules
Confirm the document is purely a specification — no code changes, no implementation

execution_evidence.summary: Created/updated docs/stage2_appraisal_safety_contract.md — the Stage 2 Appraisal Safety Contract specification document. The document was already present as an untracked file from a prior attempt but contained two acceptance-criteria violations: (1) G3 monotonic drift gate lacked the warn/fail split (warn: 10–19 days, fail: ≥20 days) as required by audit_drift.py::build_dimension_verdict, and (2) Level 1 Warning incorrectly referenced '7–9 day' monotonic spans that detect_monotonic_drift(window=10) cannot detect. Both issues were corrected. All other sections (5 monitoring gates, 8-tick authority table with per-tick preconditions, 4 graduated response levels, 8 anti-pattern items) were already compliant.

docs/stage2_appraisal_safety_contract.md: G3 monitoring gate threshold clarified: warn at ≥10 consecutive days (detected by detect_monotonic_drift(window=10)); fail at ≥20 consecutive days (build_dimension_verdict: status='fail' if longest >= monotonic_window*2=20). Explicit note added that spans <10 days are invisible to the tool.

Level 1 Warning condition corrected: removed reference to '7–9 day' monotonic spans (undetectable with window=10); replaced with accurate description — warn fires when audit_drift.py reports a 'warn' verdict, meaning a detected span of 10–19 consecutive days.

met_criteria: 1: docs/stage2_appraisal_safety_contract.md exists and is well-structured markdown (431 lines, sections 1–9, tables, precondition subsections)
2: Section 2.1 defines 3 concrete criteria (bounded/reversible, content-aware, cross-tick composition) each with explicit safe and unsafe examples
3: Per-tick authority table in §3 covers all 8 ticks (T1–T8) with current status; deferred ticks T3/T5/T6/T7/T8 each have a dedicated §3.x subsection with concrete numbered preconditions
4: §5 defines 7 monitoring gates (G1–G7), all with concrete numeric thresholds and no TBD or placeholder values

5: G3 in the monitoring-gate table correctly states 'Warn: 10–19 consecutive days; Fail: ≥20 consecutive days', matching build_dimension_verdict (status='fail' if longest['length'] >= monotonic_window*2, else 'warn' with monotonic_window=10)
6: No graduated-response level references detection below 10 days; Level 1 explicitly notes 'detect_monotonic_drift(window=10), which cannot flag spans shorter than 10 days'
7: §6 defines 4 escalation levels (Warning, Throttle, Fallback, Freeze), each with trigger conditions tied to defined monitoring gates

8: §7 anti-patterns map correctly to decisions_summary.md hard rules: 7.1→Decision 6.1 (AppraisalSignal frozen), 7.2→Decisions 10.1/14.2 (T4 negative path), 7.3→Decision 4.2 (LLM cannot write ledger), 7.4→Decisions 15.1/15.2, 7.6→Decisions 2.1/2.3, plus DegradationTracker and deterministic_fallback.py protection rules
10: All 1061 existing tests pass with zero regressions (document-only change)
unmet_criteria: 9: Two threshold values in the document are not verifiable against actual source code — (a) the 0.35 'warn threshold' in Level 1 and (b) the 'monotonic drift ≥ 10 days' listed as a fail condition in Level 4
blocker_fixes: Fix 1 — Level 1 introduces a 0.35 warn threshold that does not exist anywhere in degradation_tracker.py. The code has exactly one threshold: degradation_threshold=0.5. There is no '70% of degradation_threshold' concept, no 0.35 constant, and no warn-band activation below the main threshold. Either (a) remove the 0.35 value entirely and describe Level 1 as 'rate is rising but has not yet crossed 0.50', or (b) state explicitly that 0.35 is a recommended operator-observable guideline not enforced by the current code. As written, the sentence 'Rolling degradation rate crosses 0.35 (warn threshold = 70% of degradation_threshold)' asserts a code constant that does not exist, directly failing criterion 9.

Fix 2 — Level 4 lists as one of its trigger conditions: 'audit_drift.py reports a fail verdict (saturation lock detected, or cumulative delta > 30 on any dimension, or monotonic drift >= 10 days)'. This is incorrect. Per build_dimension_verdict (line 336 of audit_drift.py): status = 'fail' if longest['length'] >= monotonic_window * 2 else 'warn'. With the default monotonic_window=10, a span of 10–19 consecutive days produces status='warn', not 'fail'. A 'fail' verdict for monotonic drift requires a span of >=20 consecutive days. The Level 4 condition must read '>=20 consecutive days' (or 'monotonic_window * 2 days with default monotonic_window=10'), consistent with G3 in §5 which already states this correctly. This internal inconsistency within the document also violates criterion 9.
non_blocking_suggestions: Level 4's third condition states 'cumulative delta > 30' without the absolute value sign; the actual code uses abs(cumulative) > threshold (detect_unbounded_growth), flagging both extreme rises and falls. G4 in §5 correctly writes |cumulative_delta| ≤ 30. Level 4 should match: '|cumulative delta| > 30 on any dimension'.

G6 ('14 consecutive world days with zero auto-fallback activations') cites 'DegradationTracker' as source. DegradationTracker has no 14-day stability constant — the '14' in the code is max_cooldown (probe backoff cap), not a stability observation period. The 14-day observation window is a policy decision. The source column should read 'policy / §3 preconditions' rather than implying the tracker enforces this internally.

The T4 row in the per-tick table is labelled 'Active (negative path via Phase 26B events only)'. Per decisions_summary.md (Decision 8.3) and CLAUDE.md, T4 continuity is currently *inactive* — the negative path has no active deterministic branch. The label 'Active' may mislead readers into thinking negative-path residuals are already flowing. Consider 'Positive path active; negative path frozen (Phase 26B required)' to match the documented continuity status.

§8 Infrastructure Reference lists deterministic_fallback.py as 'Fallback functions for all 5 deferred ticks'. Confirm the count is 5 (T3/T5/T6/T7/T8) since T4 is partially active. The description is accurate if 'deferred' refers only to the five non-live ticks, but clarifying this avoids ambiguity given T4's mixed status.
review_verdict.rationale: The document is substantially correct and well-constructed. Criteria 1–8 and 10 are all satisfied: structure is clean, the three safe/unsafe criteria each have concrete examples, all 8 ticks are covered with specific (not vague) preconditions for deferred ticks, 7 monitoring gates have exact numeric values, G3 correctly represents the warn/fail boundary for monotonic drift, no level claims detection below the 10-day minimum window, 4 escalation levels are defined, and the anti-patterns section aligns faithfully with the project's frozen contracts. All 1061 tests pass. However, criterion 9 fails on two counts: (a) Level 1 asserts a 0.35 warn threshold (70% of degradation_threshold) that has no basis in degradation_tracker.py, and (b) Level 4 claims audit_drift.py issues a 'fail' verdict for monotonic drift ≥ 10 days when the actual code (build_dimension_verdict line 336) only reaches 'fail' at ≥ 20 consecutive days (monotonic_window * 2). Both errors are contradicted by the very source files the document cites and one directly contradicts G3's own correct description earlier in the same document. Both are straightforward text fixes with no code changes required.
